text:
kai: Heads-up — nightly perf run flagged a kernel-selection regression after the autotune merge (commit 3f9b2a7). Latency up on small sequences, KV-hit paths look worse. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: saw the alert. quick glance: throughput down ~12% on seq<=64 workloads, seq>=512 unaffected. suspect routing to fp8/kern_v2 where bf16 path used to be.

sam: timeline? which change in autotuner landed this week?

kai: merged PR #1428 yesterday, autotune: prefer tensorcore fp8 path when SM>=90 OR when driver advertises FP8, added heuristic to prefer smaller-kernel even for short seqlen.

aj: that heuristic sounds risky. for small seqlen the kernel overhead dominates. do we have microbench numbers?

bench-bot: nightly: model=gpt-small, batch=8, seqlen=32
old: p50=18.3ms, p95=28.1ms, tput=520 tok/s
new: p50=26.4ms, p95=38.2ms, tput=458 tok/s
regression: +8.1ms p50 (+44%), -12% tput

ingrid: interesting — kv-cache hit ratio unchanged. suggests dispatch + kernel launch overhead, not cache thrash.

kai: i dug traces: we now pick kernel path 'tc_fp8_smallkern' for SM92+ unconditionally if driver reports fp8. On our mixed farm a subset of nodes actually expose FP8 but have older SM warps where smallkernels are slower. mapping bug?

maria: do we detect SM version separately from driver flags? our probe is: 
```
cap = query_device_capability(device)
if cap.driver_flags.has_fp8:
    flags.support_fp8 = True
if cap.sm_major >= 9:
    flags.has_tensor_cores = True
```
but there was a recent change to prefer driver_flags over sm_major for fp8 routing. that could cause us to pick fp8 on drivers that claim FP8 but hardware doesn't have tuned kernels.

sam: that explains mixed-farm regression. some nodes are newer driver on slightly older SM silicon (e.g., SM86) where our tc_fp8_smallkern isn't optimized. need to gate on sm_major+sm_minor mapping, not just driver flag.

aj: propose immediate mitigation: revert the heuristic in autotune that prefers fp8-on-driver unconditionally. instead use explicit capability matrix: (sm >= 90 && driver_flags.fp8) || (sm >= 92). fallback to bf16 path for SM in [86,89].

kai: 👍 can do revert PR and also add a unit test for device-probe -> kernel-choice mapping. i'll file now.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline: canary rollback scheduled if PR merged within 30m.

maria: also let's capture a tiny microbench harness to validate kernel launch overhead for seqlen<=64 across representative nodes. add to nightly-smoke.

bench-bot: added job 'microbench-seq32-kernel-selection' to nightly queue, will run on tags:sm86,sm92,mixed. results posted next run.

ingrid: long-term: autotuner should keep historical perf for each (device-signature, kernel) pair and only switch if new kernel yields net improvement across p50/p95 for target seqlen bins. right now it switches based on single microbench metric.

sam: agree. checklist: 1) short revert to stop regression (kai), 2) add capability matrix guard (aj + maria), 3) extend autotuner telemetry to per-device aggregated metrics (ingrid), 4) add unit tests and microbench job (kai + bench-bot).

kai: created PR #1432 to revert heuristic and added TODO for capability matrix. linking minimal patch in thread: https://git.redwood/infra/rt/compare/3f9b2a7..1432

maria: i'll own the capability matrix change. quick pseudo for detection to avoid false fp8 picks: 
```
# require both hardware SM and driver support for FP8 fastpaths
if device.sm_major >= 9 and device.sm_minor >= 2 and driver.flags.fp8 == True:
    prefer = 'tc_fp8_smallkern'
elif device.sm_major >= 9 and driver.flags.bf16:
    prefer = 'tc_bf16_fastpath'
else:
    prefer = 'generic_bf16'
```

aj: add a unit test matrix for these tuples: [(sm86,drv_fp8=True),(sm92,drv_fp8=False),(sm95,drv_fp8=True)] to ensure deterministic picks.

ingrid: logging: please include device fingerprint (pci-id, driver-version, sm_major/minor) in the autotune decisions so we can postmortem quickly.

kai: will push small logging change in the revert PR. also adding a short note in the runbook: if seq<=64 regression observed, check 'kernel_choice' and 'device_fingerprint' fields in trace.

ops-bot: reminder: incident template 'perf-regression' created: /incidents/templates/perf-regression.md

sam: thanks all — let's keep this tight, rollback first then smarter tuning. :thumbsup:

maria: assigning follow-ups: kai (rollback), aj (unit tests), maria (capability matrix), ingrid (autotuner telemetry) — will sync in 30m.
